task_1.title: Restore deprecated JSON encoder and decoder compatibility
task_1.description: Flask 2.2.1 fixes a regression in the deprecated JSON customization API so legacy integrations can still read or assign JSON encoder and decoder classes during the 2.2 deprecation window. Deprecated access now emits deprecation warnings while preserving default behavior and compatibility for extensions that still depend on these attributes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that deprecated JSON customization attributes remain usable during the Flask 2.2.x deprecation period, so applications and extensions that still access or assign `json_encoder` or `json_decoder` continue to work while being warned to migrate to the newer JSON provider API.

expectation.grounded: Flask 2.2.1 should keep `Flask.json_encoder` and `Flask.json_decoder` available as deprecated compatibility attributes. Reading or setting either attribute must emit a `DeprecationWarning`. If an app has not explicitly overridden them, reading `app.json_encoder` should return the default `flask.json.JSONEncoder` class and reading `app.json_decoder` should return the default `flask.json.JSONDecoder` class instead of `None`. `Blueprint.json_encoder` and `Blueprint.json_decoder` must also warn on access or assignment, and an unset blueprint value must continue to mean that JSON handling falls back to the app-level configuration. JSON serialization and deserialization performed through Flask's default JSON provider must continue to honor app-level and blueprint-level deprecated overrides when they are configured.
expectation.conceptual: Deprecated JSON encoder and decoder settings should still behave like usable compatibility APIs in Flask 2.2.1. Code that reads or assigns these settings should receive deprecation warnings, but legacy extensions should not break just because the application has not customized them. Default JSON behavior should remain available automatically, and blueprint-specific overrides should still take precedence only when explicitly configured.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove `json_encoder` or `json_decoder` in 2.2.1. Do not change the meaning of an unset blueprint JSON encoder or decoder; it must still defer to the application's JSON behavior. Do not stop honoring explicitly assigned deprecated encoder or decoder classes for JSON dumps or loads during the 2.2.x series.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve backward compatibility for existing integrations while keeping the deprecation path intact. Default behavior must remain stable for applications that never customized JSON handling, and existing override precedence between application-wide and blueprint-specific configuration must not regress.

behavior: Accessing `app.json_encoder` now emits a `DeprecationWarning` and returns the default JSON encoder class when no app-specific encoder override has been set.
Accessing `app.json_decoder` now emits a `DeprecationWarning` and returns the default JSON decoder class when no app-specific decoder override has been set.
Assigning `app.json_encoder` or `app.json_decoder` emits a `DeprecationWarning` and preserves the assigned class for subsequent JSON serialization or deserialization.

Accessing or assigning `Blueprint.json_encoder` or `Blueprint.json_decoder` emits a `DeprecationWarning`; when these blueprint attributes are unset, they continue to indicate that the blueprint should use the app's JSON configuration.
Flask's default JSON provider continues to apply configured deprecated encoder or decoder overrides at the app or blueprint level during JSON dumps and loads.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Flask app with no custom JSON encoder, when legacy code reads `app.json_encoder`, it should receive a `DeprecationWarning` and the default JSON encoder class rather than `None` or a runtime failure.

Given a Flask app with no custom JSON decoder, when legacy code reads `app.json_decoder`, it should receive a `DeprecationWarning` and the default JSON decoder class rather than `None` or a runtime failure.

When an application or extension assigns a custom class to `app.json_encoder` or `app.json_decoder`, Flask should emit a `DeprecationWarning` and continue using that class for the corresponding JSON operation.

Given a blueprint without a local JSON override, when deprecated blueprint JSON encoder or decoder attributes are read, they should warn and continue to represent fallback to the app-level JSON behavior.

When both app-level and blueprint-level deprecated JSON overrides are configured, JSON operations for a request handled by that blueprint should use the blueprint override in preference to the app-wide override.
